_comment: Compatibility configuration for the retained flat-estate auditor. Canonical installations use tools/estate.py through scripts/manage_estate.py.
_governed_surfaces: These are configured comparison and reported-publication destinations, not verified integrations.

surfaces.name: claude-code
surfaces.note: Flat-tree comparison destination; canonical installs use the repository tools.

surfaces.name: codex
surfaces.note: Flat-tree comparison destination; canonical installs use the repository tools.

_cloud_comment: These four cannot be read from here: publishing is a human step through a web UI or an upload endpoint, and this toolchain holds no credential for any of them. They are tracked by ledger instead. build_bundles.py hashes every bundle it writes; record_publish.py stamps those hashes against a surface once a human has published them. estate_diff.py then reports how many bundles each tier is behind. A ledger row is a publication record, not verification. It says what was last published, which is the difference between a known gap and an invisible one.

cloud_surfaces.name: claude.ai-org
cloud_surfaces.note: User-selected account or organization. Record only an upload that actually occurred.

cloud_surfaces.name: chatgpt
cloud_surfaces.note: ChatGPT skill surface. Same bundles, uploaded through the ChatGPT UI.

cloud_surfaces.name: openai-api
cloud_surfaces.note: Skills attached to an OpenAI API deployment. Published by whoever owns that deployment, so a record here is the only visibility this repo has.

_optional_surfaces.name: claude.ai-offline
_optional_surfaces.note: point at an offline export of the claude.ai bundle to diff the cloud tier file by file instead of by ledger
